title: A chart is your data, given to it the obvious way, and it moves when your numbers do
goal: A chart on a video exists to show someone's own numbers. Putting the numbers in has to be the first, obvious thing: pasting a table from a spreadsheet or dropping a CSV file gives you a chart of it, and a chart you just added asks for its numbers right away. And the motion has to come from the data: bars grow to the values, and when the numbers change partway through the video (this quarter, then next quarter) the chart moves from one set to the next. Today the user found the charts useless: they could not give one data, and what they got was some elements moving on the screen.
notes:
The user's words (2026-10-19, intake): 'also i find the charts totally useless because i can't give it data and have it animate. Having some elements that move on the screen is not what i expected.'

The shipped task animated-charts-you-can-drop-into-a-video (done 2026-10-17) PROMISED 'Data entry is simple: a small table in the panel ... that also accepts pasted tab or comma separated text'. The code is there: ChartInspector.swift (Kind, a row table with a paste button, unit, decimals, delta), shown when EditorState.chartInHand is set (EditorState+Charts.swift:14, needs the next-animated-charts flag and a title in hand), section .chart in InspectorSections.swift:75 / InspectorPanel.swift:1393. So either the user could not reach it today or it did not read as where the data goes. Reproduce before deciding which; intake did not. The model is ChartSpec in Sources/PhotonzCore/AnimatedChart.swift (kind, title, rows, max 12 rows), one set of rows per chart; data that changes over time is new model work.

Related, do not undo: a-chart-or-title-keeps-what-you-set-by-hand-when (p2, pending) and a-chart-with-negative-numbers-draws-its-bars-bel (p2, pending) touch the same model; fold or sequence them, do not fight them. A decision card is still open on the old task ('Do the six charts build in and look the way you want in a video?', keep as is vs bolder bars); the user's complaint is that the charts are not data first, which that card does not ask. Withdraw it with that reason when this task's own card goes up.

Trap: Command V on the canvas already pastes pictures and layers; text that parses as a table becomes a chart only on a video document and only when it is clearly tabular (two or more rows with a number column), otherwise paste behaves as today.
acceptance: Reproduced first, at Next defaults in the probe on a video: add a chart from the Library and from Sequence > Insert Chart, pick it on the canvas and on the timeline, and say in the task log whether the Chart section with its data table is on screen without scrolling, below the fold, collapsed, or missing. The 2026-10-17 audit (queue/audits/2026-10-17-charts-3-pasted.png) shows it right under Properties; the panel was reordered on 2026-10-19 (Layers on top), so check whether that pushed it out of reach
The numbers come first: adding a chart opens its data with the first value ready to type, in place on the chart or in the Chart section in view, never behind a scroll

Paste makes a chart: with a video open and rows copied from Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets (tab separated) or a CSV, Command V on the canvas puts a chart of that data on the timeline at the playhead, with the first column as labels and the first number column as values, and with the header row as its title when there is one. Dropping a .csv file does the same

Data that changes over time: a chart can hold more than one set of numbers along its clip (for example Q1 to Q4 for 2025, then for 2026) and moves from one set to the next. Bars grow or shrink to the new values, the line redraws, the big number counts from old to new. Setting a second set is one obvious action at the playhead, and it is editable and undoable like a key
Every bit of motion is driven by the data: no decorative movement that is not a value arriving or changing. The background may stay, but it is a background, not the chart

Visual bar, MEASURED in the audit: in a reel of a bar chart that changes from one set to another, each bar's height at the end of the change matches its new value to within 1% of the axis, and halfway through it is between old and new. Today's charts have no second set, so this fails on today's build
A walk: paste four rows from a spreadsheet as text onto a video, check a chart of exactly those labels and values lands; add a second set at 3s, play, check the bars change at 3s
Unit tests in PhotonzCore for parsing pasted and CSV data (tabs, commas, quoted fields, thousands separators, %, $) and for interpolating between sets; Scripts/test.sh passes

Audit under queue/audits/ with a reel and contact sheet named in it, so the user can judge the motion when they want to (no decision card: cards are rare now). Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

Negative numbers are drawn honestly: a Bar or Horizontal Bars chart draws a negative value as a bar running the other way from a visible baseline, to scale with the positive bars (within 2 px at 1080p), a Line chart's point goes below its baseline, and the Big Number counts to a negative number with its minus sign. A row whose colour comes from the theme shows that colour in its swatch, not a struck-through box. Today a -25 draws as a flat line on the baseline (folded in from a-chart-with-negative-numbers-draws-its-bars-bel; a walk builds 40, -25, 60 and measures the -25 bar below the line)

log.note: digest 2026-10-20: folded in a-chart-with-negative-numbers-draws-its-bars-bel (a -25 draws as a flat line on the baseline, and a theme-coloured row shows a struck-through swatch); the audit item no longer asks for a decision card

Reproduced at Next defaults (animated-charts-walk, probe, real capture /tmp/photonz-playtest/animated-charts-walk/2-bar-chart-landed-sc.png): a Bar Chart double-clicked from the Library lands picked and the Chart section IS on screen under Properties, but with the Library open below it the section gets about 190pt: Kind, the Data header and three rows show, row Q4 is cut in half, and Unit/Decimals are below the fold inside the section's own scroll. The walk itself needs a 'reveal' to reach Paste Rows. Rows wearing the theme colour show a struck-through swatch. Nothing in the chart or panel asks for numbers: the sample data (Signups by Quarter) looks finished, so a first-time user sees a moving decoration, not a place to put their data. Diagnosis: reachable but buried, and not presented as the first thing to do.

Adversarial review before building: a first-time user sees the sample chart (Signups by Quarter) as finished and never finds the data table, which sat squeezed under Properties with the Library open. A Keynote or Premiere user expects to paste a table straight in, and expects 'change over time' to be a key at the playhead. Spreadsheets put a picture of the cells on the clipboard beside the text, so paste would land a screenshot unless the table is read first. A fixed axis is needed or a chart whose numbers all double would not move at all.

Chose: a later set of numbers is a key on the chart's own clock (its numbers have fully ARRIVED at the key; the change runs 0.9s before it, ease in-out) over a change that starts at the key, because then the playhead at the key shows the numbers being typed. Chose a fixed axis across every set over rescaling per set, because a bar that grows has to visibly grow. Chose the table showing the set the playhead is in (a set whose change has begun) over a separate set picker, the way a value typed at a key edits that key.

Chose: a pasted table's later number columns become later sets (first at 3.6s, then every 2.4s, clip lengthened to hold them); a header names the chart; a unit every value was written with becomes its unit. Command V with a chart picked replaces that chart's numbers; with nothing chart-like picked on a video it lands a new chart. Paste reads the table only when it is clearly one (split by tab, comma or semicolon, two rows or more, a number column), otherwise paste does what it did.

Shipped: ChartData.swift (ChartTable reader: tabs, quoted CSV with escaped quotes, semicolons, money, thousands, percents, K/M/B, (25) negatives, year headers; ChartStep sets; ChartSpec.shown(atMS:); PhotonzDocument.chartsShown posing a chart from the numbers of each frame inside drawn(atTimeMS:), about 1ms a frame for 12 rows in debug). Negative bars, horizontal bars and line points drawn from a zero line. Chart builds now only fade words, dots, keys and cards; Big Number no longer pushes while held. Panel: Set row, Add Set diamond, swatches in their drawn colour, Chart section scrolled into view and first value focused when a chart lands. CSV/TSV drop on canvas and panel. Walk step expectDrawn gained a height claim.

Bug found and fixed on the way: posing a bar by setting its frame drew the box at its old size clipped by the new frame, so bars going up stayed put while every frame read correct. Now resized(to:). Guarded by ChartDataRenderTests (pixels against frames), which runs in the suite.
